rationale: C15 plausibly supplied concrete national-forest drafting machinery reused in the child: lands already acquired under the March 1, 1911 act are incorporated into a named national forest, lands later acquired under the same authority automatically receive the same status, and the lands are administered under the laws applicable to lands acquired under that act. This is substantially more specific than generic proclamation boilerplate. C13 and C18 contain related forest-boundary and establishment machinery, but their language is less closely aligned with the child's acquired-and-hereafter-acquired formulation.

shared_material.child_excerpt: all of such lands which are subject to the laws applicable to lands acquired by the United States pursuant to the aforesaid act of March 1, 1911, as amended, or which are hereafter acquired by the United States pursuant to that act shall be administered as the Winema National Forest
shared_material.parent_excerpt: all lands within such area which have been acquired by the ... said act of March 1, 1911, as amended, are herby added to land reserved as parts of the Chequamegon National Forest; and all such lands hereafter acquired by the United States under such authority shall likewise be added to and reserved as parts of the said forest immediately upon acquisition of title thereto
shared_material.explanation: Both provisions combine presently acquired lands and future acquisitions under the March 1, 1911 act in assigning continuing national-forest status.

shared_material.child_excerpt: shall be administered as the Winema National Forest
shared_material.parent_excerpt: All lands to which this order is applicable which have been or may hereafter be acquired under authority of the said Title III ... shall be administered under the laws, rules, and regulations applicable to national-forest lands acquired under the said act of March 1, 1911, as amended.
shared_material.explanation: The child reuses C15's administrative mechanism tying acquired lands to the legal regime governing national-forest lands under the 1911 act.

shared_material.child_excerpt: Whereas it is desirable in the interest of effective administration of the national forests that parts of the Rogue River, Deschutes, and Fremont National Forests be transferred to and administered as parts of the Winema National Forest
shared_material.parent_excerpt: certain lands adjacent to or in an area adjacent to the said forests ... [are] suitable for national-forest purposes and ... it would be in the public interest to reserve such lands as parts of the Nicolet National Forest or the Chequamegon National Forest
shared_material.explanation: Both use a forest-reorganization framework that reallocates qualifying lands to particular named national forests for unified administration.
